plan.chapterName: OpenStax University Physics, chapter 41: Atomic Structure
plan.contextChunk: This figure is a two-dimensional vector diagram of the allowed orientations of an orbital angular momentum vector. A vertical axis labeled z rises from an origin set at the left of the frame and is crossed there by an unlabeled horizontal axis. Seven olive-green arrows of identical length fan out from the origin into the right half of the plane, their tips landing on a dashed circular arc that makes their common magnitude explicit; the topmost arrow is labeled L with a vector arrow. A dashed horizontal line runs from each tip back to the z axis, which is ticked and labeled from top to bottom 3ħ, 2ħ, ħ, then the unlabeled origin, then -ħ, -2ħ, and -3ħ, so the arrows step in equal increments of z component rather than in equal angles. Four thin arcs of increasing radius sweep from the positive z axis to the four upper arrows and are labeled θ0 nearest the origin, then θ1, θ2, and θ3; the θ0 arc opens all the way to the horizontal arrow while the θ3 arc closes on the steepest one. Holding the arrow length fixed while stepping the projections in equal units shows that only a discrete set of polar angles is available to the vector.

elements: Vertical z-axis with tick marks and labels at integer increments from -l·ħ to +l·ħ
Horizontal axis representing the xy-plane projection
2l+1 olive-green vectors of length sqrt(l(l+1))·ħ fanning out from the origin
Dashed circular arc connecting all vector tips to show constant magnitude
Dashed horizontal lines from each vector tip to its corresponding m·ħ z-axis tick
Label 'L' with a vector arrow at the top vector tip
Angle arcs labeled θ_m from the positive z-axis to each vector (for m >= 0)

interactions.label: Quantum number l
interactions.teaches: Increasing the orbital quantum number l increases both the total angular momentum magnitude sqrt(l(l+1))·ħ and the number of allowed projection states (2l+1).

interactions.label: m (z-component)
interactions.teaches: Stepping through integer m values highlights specific vectors whose z-projections are exactly m·ħ, demonstrating quantization of the z-component.

interactions.label: Angle Distribution
interactions.teaches: Classical angular momentum could adopt any polar angle (continuous), but quantum mechanics restricts it to discrete orientations where L_z is an integer multiple of ħ.

demo_steps.title: Allowed states for l=3
demo_steps.narration: For l=3, the angular momentum vector has fixed length sqrt(12)·ħ but can only point at 7 specific discrete angles.

demo_steps.title: Quantized projections
demo_steps.narration: Stepping m down from 3 to 2 changes the polar angle, reducing the z-component exactly by ħ while the overall length stays constant.

demo_steps.title: Quantum vs Classical
demo_steps.narration: A classical vector could point anywhere in the continuous semicircle. Quantum mechanics limits it to these specific quantized orientations.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Flat 2D plot (axis_screen_angles: null). Z-axis maps to screen +Y (span ±6 units), horizontal axis to screen +X (span 0 to 6). Vector length R = sqrt(l*(l+1)). For default l=3, R ≈ 3.46. Vector tips are at (X, Y) = (R*sin(θ), R*cos(θ)), where cos(θ) = m/R for m ∈ {-l...l}. Vectors are olive green (#84A540) arrows. Draw dashed horizontal lines from each tip back to Y=m. Draw Y-axis ticks at each integer m, labeled 'm·ħ' (render as m with 'h' or ħ). Angle arcs: drawn from +Y axis to each vector for m >= 0; their radius increases with m (e.g. radius = 1.0 + 0.5*m). In 'Continuous Fan' mode, render a faint semi-transparent olive semicircle of radius R in the +X half-plane, showing the classical allowed region.
interactionPlan.notes: Reactively update vector lengths, tick marks, and arc labels whenever 'l' changes. Clamp the mValue slider in code so it never exceeds ±l. When a specific mValue is selected, highlight that vector (e.g., thicker or full opacity) and its projection line, slightly dimming the others to draw focus to the selected quantized state.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Button / state for allowed m values: the learner steps through m = -3 to 3, one green L vector highlights at a time and its dashed projection lands on the matching hbar tick, showing that the z component is quantized while the vector length stays fixed.
- Toggle between discrete and continuous angles: the learner switches from the seven allowed vectors to a faint continuous fan, making clear that the diagram permits only selected polar angles rather than any orientation.
- Slider for quantum number l: the learner changes l, the number of allowed projection states and the common vector length update together, revealing how angular-momentum magnitude and allowed Lz values are linked.

authoredContext:
The quantization of the polar angle for the l=3 state is shown in the figure. The orbital angular momentum vector lies somewhere on the surface of a cone with an opening angle θ relative to the z-axis (unless m=0, in which case θ=90° and the vector points are perpendicular to the z-axis).

The quantization of orbital angular momentum. Each vector lies on the surface of a cone with axis along the z-axis.

Seven vector, all of the same length L, are drawn at 7 different angles to the z axis. The z components of the vectors are indicated both by horizontal lines from the tip of the vector to the z axis and by labels on the z axis. For four of the vectors, the angle between the z axis and the vector is also labeled. The z component values are 3 h bar at angle theta sub three, 2 h bar at angle theta sub two, h bar at angle theta sub one, zero at angle theta sub zero, minus h bar, minus 2 h bar, and minus 3 h bar.

A detailed study of angular momentum reveals that we cannot know all three components simultaneously. In the previous section, the z-component of orbital angular momentum has definite values that depend on the quantum number m. This implies that we cannot know both x- and y-components of angular momentum, Lx and Ly, with certainty. As a result, the precise direction of the orbital angular momentum vector is unknown.

⚠ Figure failed to load

discrepancies: Unselected vectors, dashed lines, and angle arcs are drawn very faintly (low opacity), whereas all are uniformly solid and fully visible in the original figure
The label for the angular momentum vector L is only placed on the currently selected vector rather than at the m=2 position shown in the source
The L vector label uses a disjointed HTML arrow character construction rather than a cohesive vector symbol
evaluation.notes: The interactive demonstration is conceptually excellent and correctly calculates all angles and lengths, but fading the unselected states makes the default view visually deviate from the uniformly-drawn source figure.
action_items: Remove the opacity reduction for unselected states so all valid vectors, dashed lines, and arcs are drawn at 1.0 opacity.
Improve the L vector label by using a standard Unicode combining over-arrow (L⃗) instead of absolute-positioned HTML spans.
